clean_text: Continuing in al-Wajiz fi Kitab as-Salah abwab al-mawaqit And we have completed all of the times in which a person is to pray and the times in which it is prohibited upon a person to pray. And now the author transitions into a similar issue. And that is the places of prayer. Where is it prohibited to pray? Where? We've discussed when it's prohibited to pray. We've discussed when it is obligatory to pray. Now the author takes us into where it is prohibited to pray. Now notice how he talks about where it's prohibited to pray. But he doesn't have a chapter regarding where is permissible to pray. Because everywhere is permissible to pray. And Sahih al-Imam Muslim Jabir radi Allahu anhu narrates that the Prophet Muhammad sallallahu alayhi wasallam says fa ayy >> He says salallahu alayhi wasallam five things I have been given no other prophet before me was given. And one of those five, he says, "And the entire earth has been made a place for prayer and a place that is potentially purifying for his prayer. So, any person from my nation whom the time of prayer subdues, then wherever he is, he has at his he has at his disposal the place to pray and he has a method of purification, which means a person may make wudu with any water anywhere and if they have no water, then with dust with a site. And a person may pray anywhere, but there are a couple of exceptions from this generality. He says here, he mentions a narration in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, very similar to the narration of Jabir that I just mentioned, that the messenger of Allah sallallahu alaihi wasallam said, "I have been given virtue and esteem over the rest of all of the prophets with six things." He says, "I have been given the most comprehensive of words." Meaning the Quran, the Sunnah, they are very concise but most comprehensive. He says, "And I have been given victory." Meaning see him, his companions, his armies, right? Have been given victory by way of striking terror into the hearts of their enemies. And the >> >> And the spoils of war, the war booty, the spoils of war have been made lawful for me." Meaning for him and his his nation. And the entirety of the earth has been made a purifying place and a place for prayer for me and my nation. And I have been sent to all of the creation, meaning the human being and the jinnkind. And finally, prophethood has been ended with me. I am the seal of the prophets." This narration is in Sahih Muslim. So, all of the earth, everywhere, every place has been made a lawful, permissible praise place for me to pray. Except for a couple of places mentioned in the following narrations. On the authority of Jundub ibn Abdullah al-Bajali, he says, "I heard the messenger of Allah salallahu alayhi wasallam saying 5 days before his death, indeed those who preceded you all, meaning the nations that came before you, before the Muslimin, the previous nations, they used to and they made a habit and a tradition of making the grave sites of their prophets and the grave sites of their righteous as places of prayer." And notice he says masajid. The masjid in the Arabic language and even in the Quran, it is used to refer to a place dedicated to salah, this building. This is a masjid. It's used to refer to any place a person prays. This is a masjid. Anywhere a person prays, this is their masjid at the moment, meaning it's the place where they are making sujud, meaning making salah. And also the word masjid and masajid is used to refer to the places on the body that the person makes sujud with. Three things. Al-masjid in the Arabic language, in the Quran, in the Sunnah, when this word is used, it's used to refer to one of three things or sometimes all of three things. Number one, the dedicated buildings for prayer, for salah, a masjid. That's what usually comes into our mind when we say masjid. Number two, any place a person prays. For that time, that is its masjid. Like in the narration we just mentioned. Number three, the places of sujud on the body. So, Allah says, "Wa annal masajida lillah." He says in Surat Al-Jinn, "That the masajid, plural for masjid, belong to Allah." "Fala tad'u ma'a Allahi ahada." So, do not worship along with Allah anyone. What does this verse mean? The masajid belong to Allah. What does it mean? The masajid belong to Allah. Which one of those meanings? All of the three. Because masjid is used to refer to what? Three things. Number one, the the building that is the masjid. Number two, any place a person prays. That's a masjid. Number three, the the body parts that are used to make sujud. This is called a masjid. So, when Allah says the masajid belong to Allah," it means all of these three. The masjid that is the building, any place on the earth that you make salah, and the body parts you use to make sujud. All of these are a masjid. They belong to Allah. Right? So, do not worship along with Allah anyone else. And so, here in this narration, the Prophet Sallallahu alayhi wasallam says that "Those nations that preceded you, they would take and dedicate and designate the grave sites of their prophets and righteous, the saints, the righteous people. Someone that's known for righteousness and dies. Salihim. They would take the grave sites of their prophets, their messengers, their righteous, and they would dedicate them as places of worship." Which means what? Which means the first two meanings. Either they would go to worship Allah at the grave site, or they would actually build a building, a masjid, and make the grave in the masjid as part of the place of worship. Do you understand? If a person were to go to any grave, and then proceed to worship Allah there at that grave, right? This person has taken that grave site as a place of worship, as a masjid. That's why it is impermissible to do anything at the grave site except what is in the Sunnah of the Prophet Sallallahu Alaihi Wasallam. The Prophet Sallallahu Alaihi Wasallam would make dua there for the deceased. He would convey a salaam to the deceased. Et cetera. And because death is so scary and everybody is so scared to death, you'll find that so many innovations are brewed and cooked up at the gravesite. Everyone who has someone that dies, that person that is close to them, that person is special. They need special worship to honor them. What is that special worship? Well, whatever comes to your mind at the moment. Whatever you you know, whatever you feel like. I want to make adhan at the at the gravesite. I want to go into the grave and lay in there before that person goes in and and spend some time in there. Many innovations have been created in this area because of the nature of death, all right? It's natural, but just because something may be somewhat expected doesn't mean that it is acceptable. We will continue this tomorrow, inshallah. Subhanaka Allahumma wa bihamdik nashhadu an la ilaha illa ant. Nastaghfiruka wa natubu ilaik. Wa sallallahu wa sallam ala nabiyina Muhammad. Wa alaihi.

summary: Sh. Ali Mashhour continues his analysis of al-Wajiz fi Kitab as-Salah, transitioning from discussing prayer times to the locations where prayer is permissible and prohibited. He establishes that the entire earth is permissible for prayer based on authentic hadith narrations from Sahih Muslim, citing the Prophet's statement that he was given six distinctive privileges, including that the earth has been made a place of prayer and purification for him and his nation. Sh. Ali Mashhour then addresses exceptions to this general permissibility, focusing on the impermissibility of using grave sites of prophets and righteous individuals as places of worship, warning against innovations that have developed around gravesites due to the emotional nature of death.
